title: BJP holds Save Democracy march in Thane

tea.why: The BJP organized the march to protest growing lawlessness, mob rule, and attempts to create anarchy in society.
tea.want: Participants demanded the protection of democratic institutions, the upholding of the Constitution, and the removal of illegal immigrants from electoral rolls.
tea.changed: Nov 1: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis addressed participants at the march, accusing the opposition of undermining democracy.

summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party organized a Save Democracy march in Thane on November 1 to protest against growing lawlessness, mob rule, and alleged attempts to destabilize the country. Senior leaders, including Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, state party president Ravindra Chavan, Forest Minister Ganesh Naik, and Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav, participated in the event. The march began at Parmarth Niketan in Pachpakhadi and concluded at Talao Pali. During the rally, speakers criticized the opposition, defended the Constitution, and stated that the party would continue its struggle until illegal Bangladeshi immigrants are removed from electoral rolls.
demands: Remove illegal Bangladeshi immigrants from electoral rolls
response: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis spoke at the event, defending the party's stance, criticizing the opposition, and stating that the march was the beginning of a larger struggle against forces attempting to create chaos.

updates.text: The Thane BJP announced plans to organize the Save Democracy march on November 1 to protest lawlessness and mob rule.
The march took place in Thane, beginning at Pachpakhadi and culminating at Talao Pali with speeches from senior party leaders.
